basis: Muscle degeneration, cataracts and cardiac conduction disease define the syndrome; endocrine dysfunction, including insulin resistance and hypogonadism, affects >30%.
Benign tumour arising in nasal respiratory mucosa; adjacent-organ invasion is not typical.
Glycosylation defect with defining developmental impairment and seizures; cataracts and biochemical hepatic injury each occur in 30-79%; contractures and respiratory failure are <30%.
Ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins; gonads as hormone organs fall under metabolic_endocrine.
Basal cell carcinoma arising in skin; pigmentation does not establish another affected organ.
Inflammation of the exocrine pancreas; endocrine failure and immune-mediated disease do not characterize most patients across this umbrella.
Diabetes, optic atrophy and deafness define DIDMOAD; urinary tract dysfunction with hydronephrosis occurs in 8/10. Neurologic degeneration also qualifies but is omitted by cap.
Guillain-Barre variant causing immune-mediated peripheral and facial nerve dysfunction; facial weakness does not imply primary muscle disease.
Staphylococcal toxin disease with defining circulatory shock; acute renal injury and thrombocytopenia each affect >30%. Hepatic injury omitted by cap; transient rash excluded.
Defined as CFH-related complement glomerulopathy with renal injury and complement immunodeficiency; individual infections and associated autoimmune diseases are separate diagnoses.
Nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss; occasional vestibular dysfunction belongs to the same otologic axis.
Pulmonary cysts and neonatal pneumothorax establish lung disease; recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Diffuse astrocytic tumour arising in the central nervous system.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, brain abnormalities and ocular defects; optic atrophy and retinal dystrophy document intrinsic eye damage.
Congenital hiatal hernia displacing the gastric cardia through the esophageal hiatus; cardia here denotes stomach.
Insulin receptor disorder causing hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; frequent hypoglycemic seizures and coma do not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Primary uterine corpus tumour; the reproductive organ of origin has no axis. Mesenchymal histology does not establish musculoskeletal involvement.
Reactive elevation of blood platelets; an underlying infection or inflammatory disease is a separate cause, not intrinsic immune involvement.
Disorder of autonomic nerves; cardiovascular, digestive and urinary symptoms do not establish direct damage to those organs across this umbrella.
KMT2E-related neurodevelopmental syndrome with developmental delay, intellectual disability and hypotonia; no other organ damage established at >=30%.
Gallstones occupy the gallbladder or bile ducts, both hepatic-axis structures; pancreatitis is a separate complication.
Extraskeletal osteosarcoma arising in liver; osteoid-producing histology does not imply bone involvement.
Infectious inflammation of the inner ear; vertigo reflects vestibular injury within the otologic axis.
Intellectual disability defines this umbrella; associated organ abnormalities vary by syndrome and are not shared by most patients.
Glycolytic enzyme deficiency classified as a glucose metabolism disease; supplied evidence does not establish common damage to another organ.
